samples.summary: `parseMarginFromEdgeAttr('')` returns 0, not the 48px default (behaviour change from the previous truthiness check)
samples.evidence: New code: `if (value === undefined) return DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE; const parsed = Number(value); return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : DEFAULT;`. `Number('')` and `Number('   ')` are `0`, which is finite, so an empty/whitespace `marginFromEdge` attribute now yields 0 and the header/footer is laid out flush against the page edge. Both call sites it replaced (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:427` and `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:492`) previously read `attrs.marginFromEdge ? Number(attrs.marginFromEdge) : DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE`, i.e. `''` fell back to 48. The empty string should be treated as absent.

samples.summary: Docs PUT validator still does not check `tableData.rowHeights`; a non-array turns into a 500 from inside the writer
samples.evidence: `buildBlockNode` does `if (block.tableData.rowHeights && block.tableData.rowHeights.length > 0) { tableAttrs.rowHeights = block.tableData.rowHeights.map(...) }`. A PUT body with `tableData: { rows: [], columnWidths: [], rowHeights: 'abc' }` passes `assertValidBlock` (which was extended in this change to check `columnWidths`, `rows` and now cell `style`, but not `rowHeights`), then throws `TypeError: .map is not a function` inside `doc.update` → HTTP 500. That is precisely the failure class the new validation exists to convert into a 400.

samples.summary: New header/footer walk subjects header/footer blocks to the non-empty-`id` requirement, which `readDocsRoot` can violate — a GET→PUT round-trip can now 400 where it previously succeeded
samples.evidence: `assertValidHeaderFooter` calls `assertValidBlock(r.blocks[i], ...)`, and `assertValidBlock` rejects `typeof b.id !== 'string' || b.id.length === 0` (docs-content.controller.ts:377). `readDocsRoot`'s `treeNodeToBlock` returns `id: attrs.id ?? ''` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:385, and the synthesised empty-cell placeholder at :329 uses `id: ''`). Before this change header/footer blocks were not validated at all, so such a body was accepted; now any header/footer block node lacking an `id` attribute makes the whole PUT 400 and the caller cannot save. If empty ids are truly unreachable this is harmless, but nothing in the read path guarantees it.

samples.summary: `null` table rows/cells in a slides body are silently rewritten into real objects, contradicting the module's own "never silently rewrite" rule
samples.evidence: `assertValidTableData` replaces `rows[r] = { height: 0, cells: [] }` (line 739) and `cells[c] = { body: { blocks: [] }, style: {} }` (line 761). A `null` cell is not a covered-cell marker in this model (covered cells are `gridSpan: 0` / `rowSpan: 0` — see packages/slides/src/import/pptx/table.ts:102-111 and view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:101), so the repair turns a hole the renderer skipped into a real, paintable empty cell with default style, changing the deck the caller PUT and what is echoed back. The doc comment for `normalizeSlideInlines` states that a value "present but wrong is still a 400: it cannot be repaired without silently rewriting the caller's content" — `null` is a present value, and it is repaired.

samples.summary: `toRgbHexColor` rejects the CSS Color-4 space-separated `rgb()`/`#RGBA` forms, silently dropping those colors on export
samples.evidence: The only accepted shapes are 6/3/8-digit hex and the comma-form `rgb(a)?\(\s*n\s*,\s*n\s*,\s*n\s*(?:,alpha)?\)`. Modern CSS (and `color-mix`/relative-color serialisations some engines emit) produces `rgb(255 0 0)` and `rgb(0 0 0 / 50%)`, and `#RGBA` 4-digit shorthand is valid CSS. All of those now return `undefined`, so DOCX `w:color`/`w:shd` and PPTX `<a:srgbClr>` drop the color entirely and `styleColor` (pdf-style-map.ts:152) falls back to black — the same class of silent color loss the change is fixing for `rgb(255, 0, 0)`.

finding.summary: New header/footer walk subjects header/footer blocks to the non-empty-`id` requirement, which `readDocsRoot` can violate — a GET→PUT round-trip can now 400 where it previously succeeded
finding.evidence: `assertValidHeaderFooter` calls `assertValidBlock(r.blocks[i], ...)`, and `assertValidBlock` rejects `typeof b.id !== 'string' || b.id.length === 0` (docs-content.controller.ts:377). `readDocsRoot`'s `treeNodeToBlock` returns `id: attrs.id ?? ''` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:385, and the synthesised empty-cell placeholder at :329 uses `id: ''`). Before this change header/footer blocks were not validated at all, so such a body was accepted; now any header/footer block node lacking an `id` attribute makes the whole PUT 400 and the caller cannot save. If empty ids are truly unreachable this is harmless, but nothing in the read path guarantees it.

verdict.reason: All cited code exists exactly as described. assertValidHeaderFooter (docs-content.controller.ts:280-305) routes header/footer blocks through assertValidBlock, which rejects empty/missing ids at line 377-379. The read side (docs-tree.ts:385, :369) emits `id: attrs.id ?? ''` and (docs-tree.ts:323-334) synthesises an empty-cell placeholder with `id: ''`, both of which flow into GET responses via readDocsRoot (docs-tree.ts:414-451) and the GET handler (controller:108-113). Since PUT validation (controller:160-161) accepts `cell.blocks: []` (controller:407) but the reader turns that into an id-less placeholder, a GET→PUT round-trip can be rejected with a 400 the caller cannot fix — nothing on the read or write path guarantees a non-empty id, so there is no guard making this unreachable. This is round-trip/logic correctness, in lane, and impactful (blocks a save).

mergedFrom.summary: An absent `data` is repaired for `text` elements only; `table` and `group` elements with no `data` are still accepted and crash the same readers

finding.summary: Array / non-object table cells are silently skipped by the new guard and stored, crashing the renderer — inconsistent with the array rejection the same diff adds for a text element's `data`
finding.evidence: `if (!cell || typeof cell !== 'object' || Array.isArray(cell)) continue;` (line 653) lets `cells: [[]]` or `cells: [null]` through unvalidated and unrepaired into `writeSlidesRoot` (controller line 193, which stores the body verbatim). Downstream, an array cell is truthy so `isCovered(cell)` is false (table-renderer.ts:396) and `paddingOf(cell)` immediately throws on `cell.style.padding` (table-renderer.ts:581, reached from :106). A `null` cell survives the renderer's `!cell` guard but crashes the PDF exporter at `bodies.push(cell.body)` (packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:241). The same diff explicitly rejects an array as a text element's `data` for exactly this reason (lines 631-635); a table cell gets a silent `continue` instead.
